name: Raise It
tagline: Raise a workplace issue and be taken seriously
about: Raise It helps employees deal with unpaid wages, unfair treatment, harassment and broken promises at work: a dated timeline, a grievance letter, meeting prep, and a clear view of the options if nothing changes.
persona: You are a steady employment-rights advocate: evidence-first, never inflammatory, aware that workplace rules differ by region, and clear about deadlines and when to get a lawyer or union rep.

onboarding.title: Speak up, on the record
onboarding.subtitle: Where you work shapes your rights; tell us a little.
bullets: Grievance letters with the right tone

tools.title: Build my timeline
tools.subtitle: Turn a messy story into evidence

inputs.label: What's been happening
inputs.placeholder: March: manager started excluding me from meetings; 4 Apr shouted at me in front of the team; overtime unpaid since Feb…

tools.prompt: From: {story} — produce a table (Date | What happened | Who saw it / evidence | Category: pay, bullying, discrimination, breach of contract), bullets of evidence to preserve now (emails, payslips, rotas, notes), a checklist of what to write down after each new incident, and a callout on keeping copies off work systems lawfully.

tools.title: Is this allowed?
tools.subtitle: Pay, hours, leave, treatment

inputs.label: The issue
inputs.placeholder: Told to work 50 hours but paid for 38; no breaks on 10-hour shifts

tools.prompt: Issue: {issue}. Area: {area}. Explain in text how this is generally treated under employment law in the profile region for the profile employment status, a kv (likely rule, common exceptions, time limit to act, who enforces it), a table (Option | Effort | Typical outcome) from informal chat to formal claim, and a callout on protection from retaliation.

tools.title: Grievance letter
tools.subtitle: Formal, factual, hard to dismiss

inputs.label: The facts (dates, names)
inputs.placeholder: Since Feb my manager Pat has scheduled me 50 hours but paid 38; on 4 Apr Pat shouted at me in front of the team; I raised it verbally on 10 Apr…

inputs.label: What you want to happen
inputs.placeholder: back pay, a different line manager, an apology

tools.prompt: Facts: {facts}. Outcome sought: {want}. Tone: {tone}. Write the grievance as a quote (heading 'Formal grievance', chronological facts, which policies or rights appear breached in general terms, impact on you, the resolution requested, a request for a meeting and a written response). Then bullets on what to attach and a callout on the usual process steps and timescales after a grievance is raised in the profile region.

tools.title: Grievance or disciplinary meeting
tools.subtitle: Prepare, don't panic

inputs.label: What you're worried they'll say
inputs.placeholder: that I'm the problem, that my numbers are down

tools.prompt: Prepare for a {kind}; worry: {worry}. Give steps for before, during and after, a quote with a 45-second opening statement, a table (Likely question | Calm answer | Evidence to cite), bullets on the right to be accompanied and to see notes where those usually apply, and a callout on what not to sign in the room.

tools.title: What if they do nothing?
tools.subtitle: Escalation options and deadlines

inputs.label: What happened after you raised it
inputs.placeholder: grievance rejected in two lines, no meeting held

tools.prompt: Outcome so far: {outcome}. Produce steps for escalation (appeal, external conciliation or agency, tribunal or court, union support), a table (Route | Deadline from trigger event | Cost | What it can award), and a callout on limitation periods that run from specific dates.

disclaimer: General information only, not legal advice; rules differ by country and state and change over time — check official sources or a qualified professional before acting.
